title: ENAHPool: The Edge-Node Attention-based Hierarchical Pooling for Graph Neural Networks
summary: Weighted adjacency powers are not literal path counts on coarsened graphs; dense edge attention is not O(N). Mask support logic remains valid. Normalization domain and SD-versus-SE reporting unresolved.
limitations: No code or separate supplement acquired.
No accuracy, runtime or memory reproduction.
Run-level CV uncertainty and hyperparameter selection protocol not independently verified.
Bibliography and later revisions not audited.

problems.title: Literal path-count interpretation fails on weighted coarse graphs

claim.location: PDF6 Section3.3, before Eq13 and after Eq15
claim.text: A^h and masked Th represent numbers of walks/shortest paths.

assumptions: Nonnegative symmetric weighted adjacency from graph coarsening
Hard partition of all three vertices into two nonempty clusters
problems.check: A=[[0,0,1],[0,0,2],[1,2,0]], partition {a,b}|{c}, attention1/2 yields coarse edge3/2 although support graph has one shortest path.
problems.result: Literal count interpretation false; correct value is weighted product-sum.
counterevidence: Binary graphs do have path-count interpretation.
Weighted connectivity remains a useful valid operator.
Informal meaning 'weighted path strength' naturally resolves interpretation.

impact.not_established: No invalid support mask, operator failure or benchmark damage.

correction.text: Use sum of products of edge weights along shortest support paths.

problems.core_dependency: Coarsened adjacency interprets weighted walks as numerical strength.
problems.severity_rationale: Minor: weighted 3-node construction disproves literal unweighted path count, while support and weighted-walk interpretation remain valid.

acceptance_check.scope: Clarify weighted strength; no failure of the coarsening operation or supported reachability mask inferred.

problems.title: Dense edge-attention complexity undercount

claim.text: Node and edge attention are both O(N).

problems.check: Complete graph has N(N-1)/2 edges and N(N-1) directed coefficients; writing them costs Omega(N^2).
problems.result: Linear node-count bound false for explicit general dense edge attention.
counterevidence: Linear possible on bounded-degree sparse graphs.
Overall O(N^3) can remain valid because other terms dominate.

impact.not_established: No total cubic-bound refutation or measured runtime claim.

correction.text: O(N+|E|) fixed-width actual-edge calculation; O(N^2) dense materialization, with clear assumptions.

problems.core_dependency: Component complexity accounting within an otherwise cubic dense pooling pipeline.
problems.severity_rationale: Minor: dense edge/node attention requires at least quadratic work; the omitted term is subordinate and the stated total cubic order survives.

acceptance_check.scope: Correct component cost; no asserted runtime reproduction or total-order refutation.
